title: Swarm Intelligence Stigmergy as a Model for Emergent Agentic Behavior: When Do Safe Local Rules Produce Unsafe Global Behavior?

original_idea.quick_reasoning: Clearly addresses an AI Safety problem with a reasonably scoped approach.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Strong chain: design simulation with safe local rules -> vary conditions -> identify emergence of unsafe global behavior -> inform multi-agent safety design. Directly addresses the collective alignment failure mode.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Multi-agent simulation design is conceptually accessible but requires careful parameter design. Measuring 'unsafe global outcomes' like resource monopolization requires defining metrics. Intermediate complexity with good tooling available.

narrow_scope.reasoning: The simulation with varied density and topology is well-defined but requires multiple experimental conditions. A focused first deliverable (one topology, one set of rules) exists but the full parameter sweep is broader.

novelty_assessment.reasoning: Novelty not assessed due to partial Wave 3 completion.
